chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I say
Not of those who have incurred Your wrath, nor of those who are astray.
He said: 'They are the Jews and the Christians, and he did not answer regarding this.'

Thus, his deviation (from a direct answer) from the answer to what the questioner asked about is evidence for the dislike of this phrase, and he was not able to explicitly state his dislike due to taqiyyah (concealment) and necessity, so he turned away from his answer entirely.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Taqiyyah (concealment of belief due to fear)
key_terms.غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ: Not of those who have incurred wrath
key_terms.وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ: Nor of those who are astray

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on saying Amin after reciting Surah Al-Fatiha in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the 'those' in the phrase as Jews and Christians, subtly indicating the dislike of saying 'Amin' after it without explicit declaration due to taqiyyah. This nuanced response serves as a scholarly proof for the recommended practice of withholding 'Amin' in this context, reflecting the Imam's strategic use of brevity to convey deeper jurisprudential rulings.
